checks: For 0<t<a the m=2 predecessor gives at least 2|A_t|−1 actual strictly above-threshold fibers within conv A_t. Their layer cake integrates to 2M_r−a and empty or zero-mass levels contribute nothing.

If the b-fiber lay in the hull of the maximum fibers, convexity and anchored d-dimensional Brunn–Minkowski would give volume at least a. A linear functional strictly separates it above that hull, and its midpoint with a maximizing q stays outside the hull.

Same parity makes the extra midpoint integral. Its volume is at least c=((a^(1/d)+b^(1/d))/2)^d, with b<c<a. For each b<t<c the same-class threshold set is exactly Q, so the extra midpoint adds one beyond the baseline inside conv Q. Integrating gives c−b.
The proof uses actual fibers of the compact convex set E, so applying it to a compact closed cap keeps all boundary contributions and the same volume convention.
Original bbc972e469554176 opening inequality and §1 have the same b=max below a and exact increment. The accepted residue-level predecessor replaces its historical layer-count citation.
